# Headers
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/api-reference/headers

Every request header, query parameter and response header the API uses.

## Request headers

| Header | Required | Applies to | Description |
| - | :-: | - | - |
| `Authorization` | Yes | All endpoints | `Key <key-id>:<key-secret>`. See [Authentication](/docs/authentication). |
| `Content-Type` | For a body | Requests with a JSON body | `application/json`. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | No | Generation requests | 1–255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID is recommended. Retrying with the same key returns the original request instead of creating a new one. See [Idempotent requests](/docs/concepts/idempotency). |
| `Hf-Expires-After` | No | Generation requests | Seconds to keep the request's data after it finishes, from 3600 to your account retention. It can only shorten retention; out-of-range values return `422`. See [Data retention and deletion](/docs/enterprise/data-retention). |

`hf-api-key` and `hf-secret` are accepted as a legacy alternative to `Authorization`. New integrations should use `Authorization`.

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Applies to | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `hf_webhook` | Generation requests | URL-encoded HTTPS endpoint that receives the result when the request finishes. See [Webhooks](/docs/how-to/webhooks). |

## Response headers

| Header | Returned | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `X-Correlation-ID` | Every response | Identifier Higgsfield assigns to this API call. Record it with the `request_id` and include both when contacting [support](/docs/help/support). |
| `Retry-After` | `429` responses | Seconds to wait before retrying. See [Rate limits](/docs/concepts/rate-limits). |
| `Cache-Control: no-store` | `403` responses for a disabled or expired API key | Do not cache the error. |

## Webhook delivery headers

Sent by Higgsfield with every [webhook](/docs/how-to/webhooks) delivery to your endpoint.

| Header | Description |
| - | - |
| `webhook-id` | Event identifier, the same across retries of one event. Use it to deduplicate. |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix time in seconds when the delivery was signed. |
| `webhook-signature` | One or more space-separated `v1,<base64>` signatures. See [Verify signatures](/docs/how-to/webhooks#verify-signatures). |
| `X-Webhook-Secret-Key` | Legacy: the secret passed with the webhook in the request body, for integrations that set one. It will be retired; verify signatures instead. |


# API reference
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/api-reference/overview

Reference for Higgsfield image and video generation operations, request status, and cancellation.

The API reference is generated from the public OpenAPI specification. It includes model-specific generation schemas plus the shared status and cancellation operations.

**Base URL:** `https://api.higgsfield.ai`

All endpoints require the [`Authorization` header](/docs/authentication). Generation submissions also accept an optional [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency) for safe retries.

Use the generation endpoint available to your account. Use **Get request status** in the sidebar to retrieve state and output for an existing request. Use **Cancel a queued request** to stop work that has not started processing.

For the complete integration flow, start with the [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) and [Requests and lifecycle](/docs/concepts/requests).


# Cancel a queued request
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/api-reference/requests/cancel-a-queued-request

/openapi.json post /requests/{request_id}/cancel
Cancel a request that has not started processing. A successful response has no body.



# Delete request data
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/api-reference/requests/delete-request-data

/openapi.json delete /requests/{request_id}
Delete a finished request's input and output files, prompt and parameters now, regardless of its retention. Billing records are kept. Repeating the call returns the same response.



# Get request status
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/api-reference/requests/get-request-status

/openapi.json get /requests/{request_id}/status
Retrieve the current state and output of a generation request.



# Authentication
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/authentication

Authenticate server-side API requests with your Higgsfield key and secret.

Create and manage API credentials in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai). Each credential consists of a key ID and a secret.

## Authorization header

Send both values in the `Authorization` header:

```http theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
Authorization: Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/status \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```

The API also accepts the legacy `hf-api-key` and `hf-secret` headers. New integrations should use the `Authorization` header.

## Keep credentials server-side

> [!WARNING]
>
> Do not call the API directly from browser or mobile application code. Anyone who can inspect the application can extract its API secret and use your account.

* Store credentials in a secrets manager or encrypted environment variables.
* Use separate credentials for development and production.
* Never include credentials in URLs, logs, screenshots, or support messages.
* Rotate a credential immediately if it may have been exposed.

## Authentication errors

Missing, malformed, or invalid credentials return `401 Unauthorized`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "detail": "Invalid credentials"
}
```

Authentication identifies the account, but individual models may have separate access restrictions. A model unavailable to the authenticated account can return `404`, `423`, or `503` depending on its operational state.


# Billing and retention
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/billing-and-retention

Understand charging, refunds, estimation, and output retention.

Higgsfield charges successful generation requests to your account balance. The exact cost depends on the selected model and parameters.

## Balance expiration

Funds added to your account balance expire one year after they are added. Plan purchases and usage with this expiration period in mind.

## Estimate a request

Use the estimate endpoint with the same model parameters before submitting generation:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/estimate/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight"
  }'
```

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "usd": "0.094"
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The values above illustrate the response format. Use the estimate returned for your authenticated account as the authoritative amount.

## Failed and moderated requests

Requests ending as `failed` or `nsfw` are not charged. If an amount was reserved when the request was accepted, it is refunded automatically.

## Canceled requests

A request can be canceled only before processing starts. A successfully canceled queued request is refunded.

## Output retention

Request files are kept for seven days after the request finishes, then deleted. The status response and the webhook include `expires_at`, the time of deletion. Download completed files to your own storage for long-term retention.

To keep data for less time, send the `Hf-Expires-After` header (one hour or more) or ask Higgsfield to set a retention period for your account. To remove a finished request immediately, call `DELETE /requests/{request_id}`. Billing records are kept in both cases. See [Data retention and deletion](/docs/enterprise/data-retention).


# Errors and retries
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/errors

Handle synchronous API errors and terminal generation failures.

Errors can occur before a request is accepted or later during generation.

## Synchronous errors

Most HTTP errors use the FastAPI error envelope:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "detail": "Invalid credentials"
}
```

Validation errors may return a list in `detail`. Do not parse human-readable messages to make permanent business decisions.

| Status | Typical meaning | Retry? |
| - | - | :-: |
| `400` | Invalid parameters or rejected input | After correcting the request |
| `401` | Missing or invalid credentials | No |
| `403` | Insufficient balance | After adding funds |
| `404` | Request or model not found for this account | No |
| `409` | The request is still running; for example, deleting a request that is `queued` or `in_progress` | After it finishes |
| `422` | Request validation failed, an idempotency key was reused with different parameters, or `Hf-Expires-After` is out of range | No |
| `423` | Model is temporarily blocked | Later |
| `429` | The account's generation queue is full (`account_queue_full`) or an endpoint limit was reached; see [Rate limits](/docs/concepts/rate-limits) | After `Retry-After` |
| `500` | Unexpected server error | Yes, with backoff |
| `503` | Model is disabled or not ready, or queue admission is temporarily unavailable (`admission_control_unavailable`) | Later, with backoff |

## Terminal failures

An accepted request can later finish with `failed` or `nsfw`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "failed",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "error": "Generation failed"
}
```

Failed and NSFW requests are not charged; any reserved amount is refunded.

## Safe retry policy

* Retry `GET` status requests after network failures and `5xx` responses.
* Do not retry authentication or validation failures without changing the request.
* Use exponential backoff with jitter.
* Set maximum attempts and a total retry deadline.
* Send an [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency) with every generation submission.
* After an ambiguous timeout, network failure, or `5xx`, repeat the same generation request with the same idempotency key.

Every API response includes an `X-Correlation-ID` header. Record it with the `request_id` and include both when contacting support.


# File uploads
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/file-uploads

Upload images, video, or audio for use as model input.

Use a presigned upload URL when your input media is not already available through a public HTTPS URL.

## 1. Create an upload URL

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
UPLOAD=$(curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body \
  --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/files/generate-upload-url \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"content_type":"image/jpeg"}')

echo "$UPLOAD" | jq
```

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "public_url": "https://cdn.example.com/input/example.jpeg",
  "upload_url": "https://storage.example.com/presigned-upload-url",
  "content_type": "image/jpeg",
  "upload_headers": {
    "Content-Type": "image/jpeg",
    "x-amz-tagging": "retention=temporary"
  }
}
```

The upload URL expires after one hour.

## 2. Upload the file

Send the file to `upload_url` with every header returned in `upload_headers`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request PUT \
  --url "$(echo "$UPLOAD" | jq --raw-output '.upload_url')" \
  --header "Content-Type: $(echo "$UPLOAD" | jq --raw-output '.upload_headers["Content-Type"]')" \
  --header "x-amz-tagging: $(echo "$UPLOAD" | jq --raw-output '.upload_headers["x-amz-tagging"]')" \
  --upload-file ./input.jpg
```

Do not send Higgsfield API credentials to the presigned storage URL.

## 3. Use the public URL

Pass `public_url` in the model parameter that accepts an input URL, such as `image_url`, `video_url`, or `audio_url`.

## Supported content types

* `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `image/gif`
* `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`
* `video/mp4`

The content type used for the upload must match the value used to create the presigned URL.


# Idempotent requests
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/idempotency

Retry generation submissions safely without creating duplicate requests.

Generation submissions accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header. Use it when a network failure or timeout leaves you unsure whether a request was accepted.

Generate one unique key for each intended generation and keep it until you receive the initial response:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
export IDEMPOTENCY_KEY=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: ${IDEMPOTENCY_KEY}" \
  --data '{
    "prompt": "A quiet alpine lake at sunrise, editorial photography"
  }'
```

If the response is lost, repeat the same request with the same key. Higgsfield returns the original `request_id` without creating or charging for another generation.

## Key rules

* Keys must contain 1–255 visible ASCII characters without whitespace. UUIDs are recommended.
* A key identifies one generation intent within your account. API key rotation does not change that identity.
* Reuse the key only when the endpoint, JSON body, webhook, and [`Hf-Expires-After`](/docs/enterprise/data-retention) header are unchanged.
* JSON object field order does not matter. Array order, omitted fields, explicit `null` values, and different URLs do matter.
* A completed, failed, NSFW, or canceled request keeps its identity. Retrying does not restart it.
* A request rejected before acceptance, such as an authentication or validation failure, does not consume the key.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Create a new key when you deliberately want a new generation, even if its parameters are identical to an earlier request.

## Parameter mismatch

Reusing a key with different request parameters returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "detail": "Idempotency-Key was already used with different request parameters"
}
```

Do not handle this response by generating a new key automatically. First determine whether the changed request represents a deliberate new generation or a client bug.

## Retry after an ambiguous failure

1. Create the key before sending the generation request.
2. Store the key with your local operation or job record.
3. After a network error, timeout, or `5xx`, retry the same endpoint and parameters with the same key.
4. Store the returned `request_id` and use its `status_url` for subsequent checks.

The replay response is an acceptance receipt and can contain `"status": "queued"` even when the original request has already finished. Read `status_url` for its current status and output.

Idempotency keys apply to generation submission endpoints in the Model API reference. Status polling, cancellation, uploads, estimates, and webhook deliveries use their existing retry behavior.


# Polling
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/polling

Poll request status without creating unnecessary load or duplicate generations.

Poll the `status_url` returned by the submission response until the request reaches a terminal state.

## Recommended strategy

1. Start with a two-second interval.
2. Increase the interval gradually up to ten seconds.
3. Add random jitter when many workers poll concurrently.
4. Stop on `completed`, `failed`, `nsfw`, or `canceled`.
5. Set an application-level timeout appropriate for the selected model.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import random
import time

import httpx

terminal_statuses = {"completed", "failed", "nsfw", "canceled"}
delay = 2.0

while True:
    response = httpx.get(
        status_url,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Key {key_id}:{key_secret}"},
        timeout=30,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    result = response.json()

    if result["status"] in terminal_statuses:
        break

    time.sleep(delay + random.uniform(0, 0.5))
    delay = min(delay * 1.5, 10.0)
```

## Retry decisions

| Response | Recommended action |
| - | - |
| `200` with a non-terminal status | Continue polling with backoff. |
| `401` | Stop and fix the credentials. |
| `404` | Stop and verify the request ID and account. |
| `5xx` or network failure | Retry the status request with exponential backoff. |

For long-running production workloads, use [webhooks](/docs/how-to/webhooks) and keep polling as a recovery path.


# Rate limits
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/rate-limits

Design integrations for account and model concurrency limits.

Rate limits depend on the account and the selected model. View the limits assigned to your account in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai).

The primary generation limit is concurrency: the number of requests that may be processing at the same time. Some models can also have model-specific limits.

## When concurrency is reached

Generation requests above your concurrency limit are still accepted. The API returns a `request_id` with status `queued`, and the request starts automatically when one of your running requests reaches a terminal status.

## When the queue is full

The number of generations waiting to start is limited too. The queue limit is a multiple of your account's concurrency limit, and each output of a batch request counts separately. When the queue is full, a new generation request is rejected with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header, and nothing is created or charged:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "detail": {
    "code": "account_queue_full",
    "message": "Too many queued generations for this account",
    "retryable": true,
    "limit": 40,
    "retry_after_seconds": 30
  }
}
```

`limit` is the queue limit for your account. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds and submit again with the same [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency); queued requests leave the queue as soon as they start.

If queue admission is briefly unavailable, the API returns `503 Service Unavailable` with `"code": "admission_control_unavailable"` and `"retryable": true`. Retry with backoff.

## Endpoint-specific limits

Some non-generation endpoints reject requests above their limit instead of queuing them. They return `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header:

| Endpoint | Limit |
| - | - |
| `POST /v1/custom-references` | Number of Soul ID references training at the same time |

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "detail": "Maximum number of concurrent requests (2) has been reached"
}
```

## Client recommendations

* On `429`, wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After` before submitting again.
* Limit generation submissions with a worker pool or semaphore so the queue stays short and never reaches its limit.
* Track each accepted `request_id` until it becomes terminal.
* Use backoff and jitter instead of retrying in a tight loop.
* Keep polling traffic separate from generation submission concurrency.
* Let us know in [Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9) before a planned traffic increase if you need higher limits.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Successful responses do not yet include rate-limit headers with your remaining capacity. Treat the limits shown in your dashboard as the authoritative values for your account.


# Requests and lifecycle
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/requests

Understand asynchronous generation requests and their terminal states.

Generation is asynchronous. A successful submission creates a request and returns immediately while the work continues in the background.

## Request lifecycle

| Status | Terminal | Meaning |
| - | :-: | - |
| `queued` | No | The request is waiting to start and may still be canceled. |
| `in_progress` | No | Generation has started and can no longer be canceled. |
| `completed` | Yes | Output URLs are available in the response. |
| `failed` | Yes | Generation failed. The response may include an `error`. |
| `nsfw` | Yes | Input or output was rejected by content moderation. |
| `canceled` | Yes | The request was canceled before processing started. |

Store the `request_id` as soon as a request is accepted. It is the stable identifier used by polling, cancellation, webhook deduplication, and support.

> [!TIP]
>
> Send an [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency) with generation submissions so an ambiguous timeout can be retried without creating a duplicate request.

## Initial response

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "queued",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "status_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/status",
  "cancel_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/cancel",
  "expires_after": 604800
}
```

Use the URLs from the response instead of constructing them manually. `expires_after` is how long, in seconds, the request's data is kept after it finishes. See [Data retention and deletion](/docs/enterprise/data-retention).

## Completed output

The output field depends on the model's output type.

```json Image theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "completed",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-31T12:05:12.481Z",
  "images": [
    { "url": "https://cdn.example.com/image-1.jpg" },
    { "url": "https://cdn.example.com/image-2.jpg" }
  ]
}
```

```json Video theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "completed",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "video": {
    "url": "https://cdn.example.com/video.mp4"
  }
}
```

```json Audio theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "completed",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "audio": {
    "url": "https://cdn.example.com/audio.mp3"
  },
  "audios": [
    { "url": "https://cdn.example.com/audio.mp3" }
  ]
}
```

Some video and 3D operations can return additional artifacts such as `zip`, `mov`, `jsx`, `fbx`, or `ply`.

Once a request finishes, its status response includes `expires_at`: the time after which its files are deleted and output URLs stop working.

## Cancel a request

Cancellation is available only while every job in the request remains queued.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${REQUEST_ID}/cancel" \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```

A successful cancellation returns `202 Accepted` with an empty body. If processing has started, the API returns `400 Bad Request`.

## Delete a request

Delete a finished request's files, prompt and parameters immediately:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request DELETE \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${REQUEST_ID}" \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```

The API returns `200 OK` with `{"request_id": "...", "status": "deleted"}`, also when the request was already deleted. A request that is still `queued` or `in_progress` returns `409 Conflict`. Billing records are kept.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Request data is kept for seven days after the request finishes, or less if you [shorten the retention](/docs/enterprise/data-retention). Copy completed media to your own storage if you need it for longer.


# Access control
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/access-control

Single sign-on, organization roles and the API key lifecycle.

## Single sign-on

Organization members can sign in to Higgsfield Console through your identity provider with SAML: Okta, Microsoft, or a custom SAML provider. SSO is configured per organization by members with the **Manage SSO** permission. See [Managing members](/docs/organizations/managing-members#enterprise-sso) for the setup steps.

## Roles

Organizations have two roles: **Admin** manages security, billing and membership; **Member** builds with the API and monitors it. See [Organizations and roles](/docs/enterprise/organizations#permissions) for the full permission matrix.

## API keys

API keys authenticate server-side requests. Each key belongs to an account, personal or organization, and everything it creates is billed to that account. In an organization, only admins can create, edit, disable or delete keys.

Create and manage keys in **API keys** in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai):

* **Name** each key after the service or environment that uses it.

* **Expiration**: set an expiration date. An expired key returns `403 Forbidden`:

  ```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
  {
    "code": "api_key_expired",
    "detail": "This API key has expired.",
    "expires_at": "2026-09-21T12:00:00Z"
  }
  ```

* **Last used**: see when each key last authenticated, to find unused keys.

* **Tags**: group keys by team, product or environment.

* **Disable or delete** a key to revoke it. A disabled key returns `403 Forbidden` with `code` `api_key_disabled`.

Usage analytics can be broken down by API key; see [Usage and billing](/docs/enterprise/usage-and-billing).

### Recommended practice

* Use separate keys for development, staging and production.
* Store secrets in a secrets manager; never in client-side code, URLs or logs. See [Authentication](/docs/authentication).
* Rotate a key by creating a new one, deploying it, and then deleting the old one.
* Set an expiration date on keys issued for temporary integrations or contractors.


# Capacity and concurrency
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/capacity

How generation limits work and how to get more capacity.

Generation capacity is measured in concurrency: the number of requests that can be processing at the same time. Your limits are shown in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai).

## How limits apply

* **Account concurrency** covers requests across all models of the account.
* **Model concurrency**: some models have a separate limit of their own, independent of the account limit.
* **Above the concurrency limit**, generation requests are still accepted. They return a `request_id` with status `queued` and start automatically as soon as one of your running requests finishes. You do not need to retry them.
* **Queue limit**: the number of generations waiting to start is capped at a multiple of your concurrency limit, counting each output of a batch. When the queue is full, new generation requests return `429 Too Many Requests` with `"code": "account_queue_full"`, the account's queue `limit` and a `Retry-After` header; nothing is created or charged. See [When the queue is full](/docs/concepts/rate-limits#when-the-queue-is-full).
* Some non-generation endpoints reject requests above their own limit with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header. See [Rate limits](/docs/concepts/rate-limits).

## Plan for scale

* Submit through a worker pool or semaphore sized to your concurrency, so the queue stays short, latency stays predictable and the queue limit is never reached.
* On `429`, wait for `Retry-After` and resubmit with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
* Track every accepted `request_id` until it reaches a terminal status, with [webhooks](/docs/how-to/webhooks) and [polling](/docs/concepts/polling) as a fallback.
* Send an [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency) with every submission so retries after timeouts never create duplicates.

## More capacity

Higher limits and dedicated capacity, isolated from other customers' traffic, are available for enterprise workloads. Email [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai) or contact your account manager before a planned traffic increase, with the models and the expected peak number of concurrent requests.


# Data retention and deletion
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/data-retention

Control how long request inputs and outputs are stored, and delete a request on demand.

Every generation request stores the files you send and the files it produces. You decide how long they are kept: seven days by default, or as little as one hour. You can also delete a finished request at any time.

## Retention periods

| Source | Range | Applies to |
| - | - | - |
| Default | 7 days | Every request |
| Account retention | 1 hour to 7 days | Every new request of the account: a personal account or an organization. Configured by Higgsfield on request. |
| `Hf-Expires-After` header | 3600 seconds to your account retention | One request; it can only shorten the period |

Retention counts from the moment the request finishes (`completed`, `failed`, `nsfw` or `canceled`), so a long generation does not eat into the time you have to download its result. The period is fixed when the request is created: changing the account retention later does not affect existing requests.

## Set retention for a request

Send `Hf-Expires-After` with the number of seconds to keep the request after it finishes:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Hf-Expires-After: 3600" \
  --data '{
    "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight"
  }'
```

The response confirms the period that applies:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "queued",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "status_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/status",
  "cancel_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/cancel",
  "expires_after": 3600
}
```

* A value below 3600 or above your account retention returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
* The header is part of the [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency) fingerprint: retry with the same value.
* The header applies to generation requests for the models in the [Model API reference](/docs/models).

## When data expires

Once a request finishes, the [status response](/docs/concepts/requests) and the [webhook](/docs/how-to/webhooks) include `expires_at`, the time after which its data is deleted:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "completed",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-24T13:05:12.481Z",
  "images": [
    { "url": "https://cdn.example.com/image-1.jpg" }
  ]
}
```

Download the output before `expires_at`. After it, output URLs stop working. The status endpoint keeps returning the request with its status, but the files are gone.

> [!WARNING]
>
> With retention shorter than the webhook retry window, a delivery to an endpoint that is down for longer than the retention period is not retried after the data is deleted. Keep polling the status endpoint as a fallback.

## Delete a request now

Delete a finished request's data immediately, regardless of its retention:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request DELETE \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${REQUEST_ID}" \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "status": "deleted"
}
```

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `200 OK` | The data was deleted. Repeating the call returns the same response. |
| `404 Not Found` | The request does not exist or belongs to another account. |
| `409 Conflict` | The request is still `queued` or `in_progress`. [Cancel](/docs/concepts/requests#cancel-a-request) it or wait until it finishes. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Deletion is temporarily unavailable. Retry later with backoff. |

## What is deleted

When a request expires with retention shorter than seven days, or when you delete it:

| Deleted | Kept |
| - | - |
| Output files: images, videos, audio and other artifacts | Request ID, model, status and timestamps |
| Input files Higgsfield stored for the request | Cost and billing records |
| The prompt and other request parameters | |
| The webhook URL and its secret | |

With the default seven-day retention, the request's files are deleted after seven days; the prompt and parameters stay with the request record. Use a shorter retention or `DELETE` to remove them too.

Billing records stay, so usage reports and invoices are not affected by deletion.

Files you upload with [file uploads](/docs/concepts/file-uploads), and copies of inputs that Higgsfield prepares for reuse across requests, are stored independently of a single request and are deleted within seven days. Requests processed by third-party model providers are also subject to the provider's own data policy.


# Model training opt-out
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/model-training

Exclude your generated outputs from model training.

A personal account or an organization can exclude the outputs it generates through the API from the data used to train Higgsfield models.

## Turn it on

1. Sign in to [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai) and select your personal account or organization.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Turn on the option to exclude outputs from training.

The setting applies to the selected account, for every API key. It is off by default. Turn it off the same way.

## What it covers

* It covers the outputs your requests generate.
* It does not change how requests are processed, priced or delivered.
* It is independent of [data retention](/docs/enterprise/data-retention): outputs are still kept until they expire or you delete them. Combine both to keep outputs for a short time and exclude them from training.


# Organizations and roles
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/organizations

How an organization shares resources, and what admins and members can do.

An organization is a shared workspace for your team in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai). Members keep their own sign-in and switch between their personal workspace and any organization they belong to with the account switcher.

## What an organization shares

Everything below belongs to the organization, not to the member who created it:

* **API keys** and every request made with them. Requests are billed to the organization.
* **Usage, analytics and request history** for all of the organization's keys.
* **Billing** details and invoices.
* **Webhook signing secret**, one per organization, covering every key and request.
* **Settings**, such as the [model training opt-out](/docs/enterprise/model-training) and the [retention period](/docs/enterprise/data-retention).
* **Enterprise SSO** connections for the organization's domains.

A personal account works the same way for one person: it has its own API keys, usage, billing, webhook signing secret, settings and retention period. Roles, members and SSO exist only in organizations.

When a member leaves the organization, the API keys they created keep working. Review and rotate keys when people change roles; see [Access control](/docs/enterprise/access-control#api-keys).

## Roles

Every member has one of two roles.

| Role | Intended for |
| - | - |
| **Admin** | People responsible for the organization: security, billing and membership. |
| **Member** | Developers and operators who build with the API and monitor it. |

Give the admin role to as few people as you need.

## Permissions

| Action | Admin | Member |
| - | :-: | :-: |
| Use the organization workspace and Playground | ✓ | ✓ |
| View usage, analytics and request history | ✓ | ✓ |
| View API keys | ✓ | ✓ |
| Create, edit, disable and delete API keys | ✓ | — |
| See whether a webhook signing secret exists | ✓ | ✓ |
| Reveal or rotate the webhook signing secret | ✓ | — |
| View billing details | ✓ | ✓ |
| Change billing details and automatic payments | ✓ | — |
| View SSO connections | ✓ | ✓ |
| Create, edit, activate, deactivate and delete SAML connections | ✓ | — |
| Invite and remove members, change roles | ✓ | — |
| Rename or delete the organization | ✓ | — |

Permissions are enforced by the API behind Console, not only hidden in the interface: a member who calls an admin-only operation directly receives `403 Forbidden`.

## Recommended setup

* Keep at least two admins so the organization is never locked out.
* Turn on [Enterprise SSO](/docs/organizations/managing-members#enterprise-sso) so sign-in to Console follows your identity provider.
* Let admins create API keys for each service and environment, and share them through your secrets manager rather than giving every developer the admin role.
* Reveal the webhook signing secret once, store it in your secrets manager, and rotate it when an admin leaves.

See [Managing members](/docs/organizations/managing-members) for how to invite members and configure SSO.


# Enterprise API
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/overview

Data controls, security, capacity and support for production integrations at scale.

The Higgsfield API gives every account the same endpoints. This section collects the controls that matter when you run it in production for an organization: where your data lives and for how long, who can access the API, how much capacity you get, how usage is reported, and how to reach us when something goes wrong.

> **[Data retention and deletion](/docs/enterprise/data-retention)**
>
> Keep request inputs and outputs for as little as one hour, or delete a request on demand.

> **[Model training opt-out](/docs/enterprise/model-training)**
>
> Exclude your generated outputs from model training.

> **[Webhook security](/docs/enterprise/webhook-security)**
>
> Verify that every delivery comes from Higgsfield and was not modified.

> **[Organizations and roles](/docs/enterprise/organizations)**
>
> What an organization shares, and what admins and members can do.

> **[Access control](/docs/enterprise/access-control)**
>
> SAML single sign-on, organization roles and API key lifecycle.

> **[Capacity and concurrency](/docs/enterprise/capacity)**
>
> How limits work, what happens at the limit and how to get more capacity.

> **[Usage and billing](/docs/enterprise/usage-and-billing)**
>
> Usage analytics in USD and invoice billing.

> **[Reliability and support](/docs/enterprise/reliability-and-support)**
>
> Status page, incident communication, support and SLAs.

## At a glance

| Area | What you get | Where to configure |
| - | - | - |
| Data retention | Inputs and outputs deleted after 1 hour to 7 days; delete any finished request immediately | `Hf-Expires-After` header, account setting, `DELETE /requests/{request_id}` |
| Model training | Generated outputs excluded from training | **Settings** in Higgsfield Console |
| Webhooks | [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) signatures with secret rotation | **Settings** in Higgsfield Console |
| Identity | SAML SSO (Okta, Microsoft, custom), Admin and Member roles with a [permission matrix](/docs/enterprise/organizations#permissions) | **Organization settings** |
| API keys | Named keys with expiration, tags and last-used time | **API keys** in Higgsfield Console |
| Capacity | Account and model concurrency; requests above the limit are queued | Higgsfield Console; higher or dedicated capacity on request |
| Usage analytics | Per-model usage and estimated cost in USD, for dashboards and monitoring | `GET /models/usage`, Higgsfield Console |
| Reliability | Public status page, correlation IDs for every response | [status.higgsfield.ai](https://status.higgsfield.ai) |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Some settings, such as an account-wide retention period, invoice billing and dedicated capacity, are configured by Higgsfield. Email [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai) or contact your account manager.


# Reliability and support
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/reliability-and-support

Service status, incident communication, support channels and SLAs.

## Service status

[status.higgsfield.ai](https://status.higgsfield.ai) shows the current state and 90-day uptime of the Developer Console, the Models API and webhook delivery, together with incident history and announcements. Select **Get updates** on the status page to be notified about incidents and maintenance.

## Build for resilience

* Retry `5xx` responses and network failures with exponential backoff and jitter; repeat generation submissions with the same [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/concepts/idempotency).
* Use [webhooks](/docs/how-to/webhooks) for completion and keep [polling](/docs/concepts/polling) as a fallback.
* Download outputs to your own storage before they [expire](/docs/enterprise/data-retention).
* See [Errors and retries](/docs/concepts/errors) for which errors are safe to retry.

## Get help

| Channel | Use for |
| - | - |
| [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai) | Account, billing, invoices and enterprise requests |
| [Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9) | Technical questions and integration help |
| Your account manager | Capacity, contracts and escalations |

Include the `request_id` and the `X-Correlation-ID` response header of the affected request, the model or endpoint, and the time in UTC. Every API response carries `X-Correlation-ID`; record it in your logs together with the `request_id`.

## Service level agreements

Uptime commitments, support response times and escalation paths are available as part of an enterprise agreement. Email [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai) or contact your account manager.


# Usage and billing
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/usage-and-billing

Usage analytics per model and API key, and invoice billing.

## Usage analytics

`GET /models/usage` returns analytics for dashboards and monitoring: the completed generations of the account the API key belongs to and their estimated cost in USD, grouped by time bucket and model.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Usage analytics is not a billing record. Data can lag behind real time and may not include every request, so totals can differ from your invoice. Use your invoices for reconciliation, and a request's status endpoint for a single request.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --get \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/models/usage \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --data-urlencode "start=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" \
  --data-urlencode "end=2026-10-24T00:00:00Z" \
  --data-urlencode "timeframe=day" \
  --data-urlencode "expand=time_series" \
  --data-urlencode "expand=auth_method"
```

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "time_series": [
    {
      "bucket": "2026-10-23T00:00:00Z",
      "results": [
        {
          "model": "higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard",
          "unit": "generation",
          "quantity": "120",
          "unit_price": "0.0940",
          "cost": "11.2800",
          "currency": "USD",
          "auth_method": "3f0c8a2e-5b7d-4e19-9a61-2c4d8e7f1a90"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "total": 23,
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 50
}
```

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `start`, `end` | last 24 hours | ISO 8601 time range, at most 31 days. |
| `timeframe` | `hour` | Bucket size: `hour`, `day`, `week` (from Monday) or `month`. |
| `bound_to_timeframe` | `true` | Align `start` and `end` to bucket boundaries. |
| `model` | all models | Filter by model; repeat for several. |
| `expand` | `time_series` | Add `auth_method` to break results down by API key ID. |
| `page`, `limit` | `1`, `50` | Pagination over buckets; `limit` is at most 100. |

Only completed generations are counted: failed, moderated and canceled requests are not charged.

## Invoice billing

Instead of a prepaid balance, enterprise organizations can be billed by invoice for their usage. Terms, pricing and payment schedule are agreed with Higgsfield. Email [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai) or contact your account manager.


# Webhook security
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/enterprise/webhook-security

Verify that webhook deliveries come from Higgsfield and were not modified.

Webhook deliveries are signed with the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) scheme. Verify every delivery before you trust its content: anyone who learns your webhook URL can send requests to it.

## How it works

| Header | Content |
| - | - |
| `webhook-id` | Stable identifier of the event. Redeliveries of the same event reuse it, so you can deduplicate by it. |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix time in seconds when the delivery was signed. Reject deliveries outside a five-minute tolerance. |
| `webhook-signature` | One or more space-separated `v1,<base64>` signatures of the raw body. |

The signing secret belongs to the account, personal or organization, and covers every API key and request. Reveal it in **Settings** in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai); it starts with `whsec_`. In an organization, only admins can reveal or rotate it. Deliveries are signed from the moment the secret is first revealed.

See [Verify signatures](/docs/how-to/webhooks#verify-signatures) for library and manual verification examples.

## Rotate the secret

Rotate the secret in **Settings** if it may have been exposed. The new secret takes effect immediately and the previous one keeps working for 24 hours. During that window every delivery carries one signature per secret, so you can deploy the new secret without dropping deliveries.

## Endpoint requirements

* The webhook URL must use HTTPS and resolve only to public IP addresses, without credentials in the URL. Other URLs are rejected when the request is submitted.
* Respond with `2xx` within ten seconds after durably recording the event. Network failures and `5xx` responses are retried; `4xx` responses are not.
* After a request's data is [deleted](/docs/enterprise/data-retention), no further deliveries are made for it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Integrations that pass a secret in the webhook request body still receive it in the `X-Webhook-Secret-Key` header. That header will be retired; switch to signature verification.


# FAQ
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/help/faq

Answers about Higgsfield API authentication, asynchronous requests, model selection, billing, limits, and output retention.

# Frequently Asked Questions

> **What base URL and authentication header should I use?**
>
> Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai` and authenticate server-side with `Authorization: Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET`. Do not use a Bearer token or expose the secret in browser or mobile code. See [Authentication](/docs/authentication).

> **Why does a generation request not return the media immediately?**
>
> Generation is asynchronous. A successful submission returns `request_id`, `status_url`, and `cancel_url`. Poll `status_url` or configure a webhook, then read the output URL after the status becomes `completed`. See [Requests and lifecycle](/docs/concepts/requests).

> **Which model or endpoint should I use?**
>
> Choose by input and output workflow: text-to-image, image editing, text-to-video, image-to-video, or frame-controlled video. Model availability depends on your account. Not sure which endpoint fits your case? Ask in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9).

> **What is the retention policy for generated output files?**
>
> Generated output files are stored and accessible for a minimum of 7 days from the time of creation. We strongly recommend downloading and storing files in your own infrastructure for long-term retention. Files may be removed from our servers at any time after the 7-day retention period.

> **Are failed requests charged?**
>
> No. Failed generation requests are not charged to your account. You are only billed for successful completions. In the event of a failure, any costs associated with that request are automatically refunded.

> **What does NSFW status mean?**
>
> NSFW (Not Safe For Work) indicates that either your input parameters or the generated output did not pass our content moderation system due to content policy violations. Content policy rules and restrictions may vary depending on the specific model being used.

> **Are NSFW-flagged requests charged?**
>
> No. Requests flagged as NSFW are not charged to your account. When content is rejected by our moderation system, any associated costs are automatically refunded.

> **Do you offer invoice-based billing?**
>
> The API runs on pay-as-you-go by default: you top up a balance and pay per generation. Invoice-based billing is available for customers on a committed-use contract. To discuss one, [contact sales](https://open.higgsfield.ai/contact-sales).

> **What are the API rate limits?**
>
> Rate limits depend on your account and the selected model. You can view your current limits and usage in your [dashboard](https://console.higgsfield.ai). Need a higher limit? Let us know in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9).

> **How do I monitor my API usage?**
>
> You can monitor your API usage, spending, and request history through the [Higgsfield Console dashboard](https://console.higgsfield.ai). The dashboard provides real-time analytics and detailed usage reports.

> **Which programming languages are supported?**
>
> We provide official Python and Node.js/TypeScript SDKs. You can also integrate directly through the REST API from any language with an HTTP client. See [Client libraries](/docs/how-to/sdk).

> **How do I get started with the API?**
>
> To get started:
>
> 1. Create an account at [console.higgsfield.ai](https://console.higgsfield.ai)
>
> 2. Generate your API credentials from the dashboard
>
> 3. Follow our [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) for your first integration
>
> 4. Read [How the API works](/docs/how-to/introduction), then use a generation endpoint available to your account

> **What happens if a generation takes too long?**
>
> Generation requests have model-specific timeout limits. If a request exceeds the timeout, it will be marked as failed and you will not be charged. You can resubmit the request. If timeouts keep happening, reach out in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9) with your `request_id`.

## Still have questions?

If you didn't find your answer, here is where to go next:

* **Discord community**: [Join the Higgsfield Discord](https://discord.gg/BEea92KeR9) and ask your question there
* **Account and billing**: email [support@higgsfield.ai](mailto:support@higgsfield.ai)
* **Documentation**: [Read the Quickstart](/docs/quickstart)
* **API Reference**: [Request endpoint reference](/docs/api-reference/overview)

# How the API works
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/how-to/introduction

Learn the common authentication and asynchronous request lifecycle shared by Higgsfield image and video models.

The Higgsfield API uses an asynchronous request lifecycle:

1. Submit JSON parameters to a model endpoint.
2. Store the returned `request_id`.
3. Poll `status_url` or wait for a webhook.
4. Download output when the request becomes `completed`.

> **[Start with the Quickstart](/docs/quickstart)**
>
> Run a complete request using cURL.

> **[Understand requests](/docs/concepts/requests)**
>
> Learn statuses, output shapes, cancellation, and retention.

**Base URL:** `https://api.higgsfield.ai`

Every request requires server-side [authentication](/docs/authentication). For production integrations, read the [polling](/docs/concepts/polling), [webhook](/docs/how-to/webhooks), and [error handling](/docs/concepts/errors) guides.


# Client libraries
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/how-to/sdk

Use the official Python and TypeScript SDKs.

Official SDKs handle authentication, submission, polling, cancellation, and file uploads. Use them only in trusted server-side environments.

> **[Python](https://github.com/higgsfield-ai/higgsfield-client)**
>
> Synchronous and asynchronous APIs for Python 3.8+.

> **[Node.js and TypeScript](https://github.com/higgsfield-ai/higgsfield-js)**
>
> Typed server-side client with automatic polling and retries.

## Python

### Install

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Configure credentials

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
export HF_KEY="your-api-key-id:your-api-key-secret"
```

### Submit and wait

```python Synchronous theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    "higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard",
    arguments={
        "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight",
    },
)

print(result["images"][0]["url"])
```

```python Asynchronous theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import asyncio

import higgsfield_client


async def main():
    result = await higgsfield_client.subscribe_async(
        "higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard",
        arguments={
            "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight",
        },
    )
    print(result["images"][0]["url"])


asyncio.run(main())
```

Use `submit` or `submit_async` when you need a request controller for explicit polling, status checks, or cancellation. The Python SDK also provides `upload`, `upload_file`, and `upload_image` helpers.

## Node.js and TypeScript

### Install

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

### Configure credentials

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
export HF_CREDENTIALS="your-api-key-id:your-api-key-secret"
```

### Submit and wait

```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard",
  {
    input: {
      prompt: "Editorial portrait in soft daylight",
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

if (result.status === "completed") {
  console.log(result.images?.[0]?.url);
}
```

The v2 TypeScript client is server-side only and blocks browser use to prevent credential exposure.

## Choose an integration style

| Requirement | Recommended API |
| - | - |
| Script or prototype | `subscribe` / `subscribe_async` |
| Worker with explicit lifecycle control | `submit` / `submit_async` |
| Existing request ID | `status`, `result`, or `cancel` |
| Production event-driven integration | Submit with a webhook and keep status polling as recovery |

See the [Python SDK repository](https://github.com/higgsfield-ai/higgsfield-client) and [TypeScript SDK repository](https://github.com/higgsfield-ai/higgsfield-js) for the complete client APIs.


# Webhooks
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/how-to/webhooks

Receive terminal generation results without continuous polling.

Pass an HTTPS endpoint in the `hf_webhook` query parameter when submitting generation. Higgsfield sends one or more HTTP `POST` deliveries after the request reaches `completed`, `failed`, or `nsfw`.

## Configure a webhook

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard?hf_webhook=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fwebhooks%2Fhiggsfield" \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight"
  }'
```

Your endpoint must be publicly reachable over HTTPS, accept a JSON request body, and respond within ten seconds.

## Payload envelope

All deliveries use the same top-level envelope. Successful output is nested in `payload`.

```json Completed image theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "9417a243-e457-4075-895b-b68f3cda5303",
  "status": "completed",
  "error": null,
  "expires_at": "2026-10-31T12:05:12.481Z",
  "payload": {
    "images": [
      {
        "url": "https://cdn.example.com/generated-image.jpg",
        "content_type": "image/jpeg"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json Completed video theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "9417a243-e457-4075-895b-b68f3cda5303",
  "status": "completed",
  "error": null,
  "payload": {
    "video": {
      "url": "https://cdn.example.com/generated-video.mp4",
      "content_type": "video/mp4"
    }
  }
}
```

```json Failed theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "9417a243-e457-4075-895b-b68f3cda5303",
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "Generation failed",
  "payload": null
}
```

```json NSFW theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "9417a243-e457-4075-895b-b68f3cda5303",
  "status": "nsfw",
  "error": null,
  "payload": null
}
```

Audio responses contain `payload.audio`. Some video and 3D operations can also include `zip`, `mov`, `jsx`, `fbx`, or `ply` artifacts.

`expires_at` is the time after which the request's files are deleted and the URLs in `payload` stop working; download them before then. See [Data retention and deletion](/docs/enterprise/data-retention).

## Verify signatures

Webhook deliveries are signed using the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) specification. Verify every delivery before trusting its contents: anyone who knows your endpoint URL can send it a request.

Each signed delivery includes three headers:

| Header | Value |
| - | - |
| `webhook-id` | Unique event identifier. It stays the same across retries of the same event. |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix time in seconds when the delivery was signed. |
| `webhook-signature` | One or more space-separated signatures in the form `v1,<base64>`. |

### Get your signing secret

Open **Settings** in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai) and reveal the webhook signing secret. It starts with `whsec_`. The secret is created the first time it is revealed; until then, deliveries for your account are not signed.

One secret covers every API key and request of the account. In an organization, only admins can reveal or rotate it. Store it with your other server-side credentials and never expose it in browser or mobile code.

### Verify with a library

Use an official Standard Webhooks library. It checks the signature and rejects timestamps outside a five-minute tolerance. Verify the raw request body before parsing JSON: re-serialized JSON does not match the signature.

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import os

from standardwebhooks import Webhook, WebhookVerificationError

webhook = Webhook(os.environ["HF_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])

try:
    event = webhook.verify(raw_body, headers)
except WebhookVerificationError:
    return Response(status=400)
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import { Webhook } from "standardwebhooks";

const webhook = new Webhook(process.env.HF_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);

let event;
try {
  event = webhook.verify(rawBody, req.headers);
} catch {
  return res.status(400).send();
}
```

Install the library with `pip install standardwebhooks` or `npm install standardwebhooks`. Libraries for other languages are listed in the [Standard Webhooks repository](https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks).

### Verify manually

1. Remove the `whsec_` prefix from the secret and base64-decode the rest to get the HMAC key.
2. Build the signed content `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`.
3. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the signed content with the key and base64-encode the result.
4. Compare it with each `v1,` entry of `webhook-signature` using a constant-time comparison. Accept the delivery if any entry matches.
5. Reject deliveries whose `webhook-timestamp` is more than five minutes from your current time.

### Rotate the secret

Rotate the secret in **Settings** if it may have been exposed. The new secret takes effect immediately, and the previous secret keeps working for 24 hours. During that window `webhook-signature` carries one signature per secret, so update your server before the previous secret expires. At most two secrets are valid at the same time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Integrations that pass a secret with the webhook in the request body still receive it in the `X-Webhook-Secret-Key` header. That header will be retired; switch to signature verification.

## Delivery and retries

* Return any `2xx` response after durably recording the event.
* Network failures and `5xx` responses are retried for up to two hours.
* `4xx` responses are treated as permanent and are not retried.
* Duplicate deliveries are possible. Deduplicate by `webhook-id`, or by `request_id` and terminal `status` for unsigned deliveries.
* If delivery fails permanently, retrieve the result through the authenticated status endpoint.
* No deliveries are made after a request's data is [deleted](/docs/enterprise/data-retention). With retention shorter than the retry window, keep polling as a fallback.

Reject request bodies that do not match the documented envelope, but acknowledge valid duplicate deliveries with `2xx`.


# Higgsfield API
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/index

Generate images and videos through one authenticated, asynchronous API.

Higgsfield provides one integration point for generative media models. Submit a request to a model endpoint, then poll for the result or receive a webhook when processing finishes.

> **[Run your first request](/docs/quickstart)**
>
> Create credentials and complete a generation from submission to result.

> **[Get an API key](https://console.higgsfield.ai)**
>
> Create and manage server-side credentials in Higgsfield Console.

## Make a request

Every model uses the same authentication and asynchronous request lifecycle. The JSON body depends on the selected model.

Start with [Genjutsu motion transfer](/docs/models/genjutsu/motion-transfer). Replace the example media URLs with publicly accessible URLs for your own video and reference image. The source video must be at least 4 seconds long.

```bash Genjutsu theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0 \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
    "image_urls": ["https://example.com/input.jpg"]
  }'
```

```bash SOUL V2 theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/standard \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "prompt": "Editorial portrait in soft daylight"
  }'
```

The API immediately returns a request identifier and links for checking or canceling the request.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "queued",
  "request_id": "d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff",
  "status_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/status",
  "cancel_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/d7e6c0f3-6699-4f6c-bb45-2ad7fd9158ff/cancel"
}
```

## Choose your path

> **[Build a prototype](/docs/how-to/sdk)**
>
> Use the Python or TypeScript SDK to submit a request and wait for its result.

> **[Ship to production](/docs/concepts/requests)**
>
> Learn the request lifecycle, polling, webhooks, errors, and limits.

> **[Upload media](/docs/concepts/file-uploads)**
>
> Upload input files to Higgsfield storage before generation.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Output files are available for at least seven days. Download completed output to your own storage for long-term retention.

# Ads Studio API

Turn a marketing brief and optional product references into 1–8 ad concepts rendered as images with GPT Image 2.5 Flare.

# Ads Studio — Generate ads API
Source: https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/models/ads-studio/generate

Generate ads with Ads Studio: request parameters, examples and response handling.

[← Ads Studio](/docs/models/ads-studio)

**Endpoint:** `POST https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/ads-studio/v1.0`

**Endpoint ID:** `higgsfield/ads-studio/v1.0`

[▶
Open API PlaygroundAds Studio · Generate ads
↗](https://console.higgsfield.ai/models/higgsfield%2Fads-studio%2Fv1.0/playground)

## Usage notes

* Submit one request with your brief. Ad concepts are prepared automatically, then rendered as images; no separate preparation or generate call is required.
* batch\_size selects 1–8 ad concepts. Each concept produces one image, so a fully successful batch returns batch\_size images.
* Rendering uses GPT Image 2.5 Flare with fixed 2k resolution and high quality. Exact dimensions depend on aspect\_ratio. quality, resolution, renderer and fallback model are not public inputs.
* All outputs in a batch use the requested aspect\_ratio. Omitting it selects 1:1. The value auto is not supported.
* Set HF\_API\_KEY\_ID and HF\_API\_KEY\_SECRET to your API credentials. Set a unique IDEMPOTENCY\_KEY for each intended generation; reuse it only when retrying that same request.

## Quick start

```bash cURL theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/ads-studio/v1.0 \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: ${IDEMPOTENCY_KEY}" \
  --data '{
  "prompt": "Create two distinct ads for a fictional herbal tea called Quiet Evening. Use a green tea tin, warm light and the headline Make time for yourself. No people.",
  "target_audience": "Busy professionals looking for a relaxing evening ritual",
  "niche": "Herbal tea",
  "language": "en",
  "aspect_ratio": "9:16",
  "batch_size": 2
}'
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import higgsfield_client

arguments = (
    {'prompt': 'Create two distinct ads for a fictional herbal tea called Quiet '
               'Evening. Use a green tea tin, warm light and the headline Make '
               'time for yourself. No people.',
     'target_audience': 'Busy professionals looking for a relaxing evening ritual',
     'niche': 'Herbal tea',
     'language': 'en',
     'aspect_ratio': '9:16',
     'batch_size': 2}
)
result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    "higgsfield/ads-studio/v1.0",
    arguments=arguments,
)
print(result["images"][0]["url"])
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({ credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS });

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe("higgsfield/ads-studio/v1.0", {
  input:
    {
      "prompt": "Create two distinct ads for a fictional herbal tea called Quiet Evening. Use a green tea tin, warm light and the headline Make time for yourself. No people.",
      "target_audience": "Busy professionals looking for a relaxing evening ritual",
      "niche": "Herbal tea",
      "language": "en",
      "aspect_ratio": "9:16",
      "batch_size": 2
    },
  withPolling: true,
});

if (result.status === "completed") {
  console.log(result.images?.[0]?.url);
}
```

## Input schema

**niche** `string`

Optional product category or business niche used to guide ad concepts.
Maximum characters: `1000`.

**prompt** `string` *required*

Required marketing brief describing the product or service, desired message and visual direction. Must contain non-whitespace text.
Minimum characters: `1`.
Maximum characters: `8000`.
Pattern: `\S`.

**language** `string`

Optional language guidance for ad copy, for example en or ru. This is free text, not a fixed language-code enum.
Maximum characters: `80`.

**batch\_size** `integer` (default: 1)

Number of ad concepts and requested output images. Billing is summed across the rendered images.
Minimum: `1`.
Maximum: `8`.

**image\_urls** `array` (default: \[])

Optional product or visual reference images. Supply up to 10 directly downloadable HTTP(S) URLs. Omit or send \[] for text-only generation.
Maximum items: `10`.
Each item: string. Minimum characters: `1`. Maximum characters: `8192`. Pattern: `^https?://`.

**aspect\_ratio** `string` (default: 1:1)

Output width-to-height ratio shared by every image in the batch.
Allowed values: `"1:1"`, `"4:5"`, `"5:4"`, `"16:9"`, `"9:16"`, `"4:3"`, `"3:4"`, `"21:9"`, `"3:2"`, `"2:3"`, `"2:1"`, `"1:2"`, `"3:1"`, `"1:3"`.

**target\_audience** `string`

Optional description of the intended audience, such as interests, needs or use cases.
Maximum characters: `2000`.

> **Complete JSON schema**
>
> ```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
> {
>   "type": "object",
>   "required": [
>     "prompt"
>   ],
>   "properties": {
>     "niche": {
>       "type": "string",
>       "default": "",
>       "maxLength": 1000
>     },
>     "prompt": {
>       "type": "string",
>       "pattern": "\\S",
>       "maxLength": 8000,
>       "minLength": 1
>     },
>     "language": {
>       "type": "string",
>       "default": "",
>       "maxLength": 80
>     },
>     "batch_size": {
>       "type": "integer",
>       "default": 1,
>       "maximum": 8,
>       "minimum": 1
>     },
>     "image_urls": {
>       "type": "array",
>       "items": {
>         "type": "string",
>         "pattern": "^https?://",
>         "maxLength": 8192,
>         "minLength": 1
>       },
>       "default": [],
>       "maxItems": 10
>     },
>     "aspect_ratio": {
>       "enum": [
>         "1:1",
>         "4:5",
>         "5:4",
>         "16:9",
>         "9:16",
>         "4:3",
>         "3:4",
>         "21:9",
>         "3:2",
>         "2:3",
>         "2:1",
>         "1:2",
>         "3:1",
>         "1:3"
>       ],
>       "type": "string",
>       "default": "1:1"
>     },
>     "target_audience": {
>       "type": "string",
>       "default": "",
>       "maxLength": 2000
>     }
>   },
>   "additionalProperties": false
> }
> ```

## Product references

Omit `image_urls` for text-only generation. To guide the ad with your product, send direct image URLs that the service can download without browser cookies or custom authentication headers. An unexpired signed HTTPS URL is suitable. Keep the URLs valid while the request is being processed.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "prompt": "Create three distinct premium perfume ads. Preserve the bottle and label. Use the headline Leave a lasting note.",
  "image_urls": ["https://example.com/product.png"],
  "target_audience": "People looking for a distinctive gift",
  "niche": "Fragrance",
  "language": "en",
  "aspect_ratio": "4:5",
  "batch_size": 3
}
```

Reference images guide generation; exact preservation of a product, label or text is not guaranteed. Supported oversized references are normalized before rendering. The output remains a PNG at the selected aspect ratio.

## Pricing

**Illustrative estimate: approximately \$0.084 per image.** This is a budgeting example, not a fixed charge or maximum price. Actual cost varies with the aspect ratio, prepared prompt, reference images and measured token usage. Consult the current model pricing in the Playground before submitting work.

| Token category | USD per 1 million tokens |
| - | -: |
| Text input | \$5.00 |
| Cached text input | \$1.25 |
| Text output | \$10.00 |
| Image input | \$8.00 |
| Cached image input | \$2.00 |
| Image output | \$30.00 |

The initial charge is an estimate reconciled to actual rendering usage on completion, with standard rounding. Cached input is charged at the cached rate instead of being counted again as uncached input. Ad concept preparation is not billed separately.

For a batch, the final price is the **sum of the actual image charges**. Do not multiply aggregated batch token usage by `batch_size` again. Three images at the illustrative estimate would budget approximately \$0.252; the actual total can differ.

## Check request status

Use the returned `status_url` with the same API credentials. Set `REQUEST_ID` to the identifier returned when you submit the request:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${REQUEST_ID}/status" \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```

Follow the shared [polling guidance](/docs/concepts/polling). A request handle confirms acceptance, not successful image generation. Stop polling on `completed`, `failed`, `nsfw`, or `canceled`, and inspect the returned outputs and errors.

## Response

Submission returns one request handle for the entire batch:

```json Accepted theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "status": "queued",
  "request_id": "REQUEST_ID",
  "status_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/status",
  "cancel_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/cancel"
}
```

A fully successful two-image batch returns two indexed images:

```json Completed theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
{
  "request_id": "REQUEST_ID",
  "status_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/status",
  "cancel_url": "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/cancel",
  "status": "completed",
  "images": [
    {"index": 0, "url": "https://example.com/ad-1.png"},
    {"index": 1, "url": "https://example.com/ad-2.png"}
  ],
  "errors": []
}
```

Process every returned image rather than only `images[0]`. Use its zero-based `index` to identify its batch slot and inspect `errors` for unsuccessful slots. After `subscribe` returns, extend the Python quick start with:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark"}}
for image in result.get("images", []):
    print(image["index"], image["url"])
for error in result.get("errors", []):
    print(error)
```

See [idempotent requests](/docs/concepts/idempotency), [polling](/docs/concepts/polling), [request errors](/docs/concepts/errors) and [authentication](/docs/authentication) for shared request handling.

Create video shots with camera and style controls and media references.

## Workflows
